title: SRE weekly ops sync — reliability review prep (2026-03-29)
content:
Purpose: quick prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync and reliability review. Focus: SLO status, paging trends last 7d, top incidents, proposed mitigations, and roll-forwards for next week.

Agenda (10:00 - 11:00):
- Quick updates (5m)
- SLOs & error budgets (15m)
- Paging trends & root-cause signals (15m)
- Top incidents review (15m)
- Action items & owners (10m)

Key metrics snapshot (last 7d):
- Request success SLO (99.9% target): 99.82% -> 0.08% error budget used -> current burn rate: medium (on track but trending up).
- 99th latency for text-gen endpoints: 520ms (target < 450ms) -> tail latency spike on 03/25-03/27 during model reloads.
- Pager rate: 18 pages / 7d (baseline 10/wk) -> +80% vs baseline.
- On-call MTTR: 24m median (improved), but long tail incidents still near 3h.

Paging trends / signals observed:
- Increased paging correlates to model reload noise after rolling quantized variants. Most pages were timeouts and degraded throughput alerts.
- Alert noise from noisy downstream auth calls (token service) contributed to ~4 pages. Follow-up with infra-auth team needed.
- Nightly cache warm-up windows cause higher tail latency for first few minutes after deployment; caching changes in staging didn't fully mirror prod.

Top incidents (last 7d) — high-level:
1) 2026-03-25 02:17 UTC — mass model reload during canary -> gg-degraded-throughput alert -> impact: increased latency and 5xx for 12m.
   - Root cause: race condition in rollout script causing simultaneous model reloads across a subset of serving pool (quantized variant deploy).
   - Mitigation applied: paused rollout, rollback of canary, hotfix to rollout script to linearize reloads.
   - Follow-ups: add rollout gating in orchestration (ticket: JIRA-SRE-987). Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-04-05.

2) 2026-03-27 18:40 UTC — intermittent 401s from auth proxy -> degraded client requests for 6m.
   - Root cause: token cache miss storm after key rotation in auth service (downstream).
   - Mitigation: retried requests, temporary bypass for low-risk clients.
   - Follow-ups: coordinate with infra-auth to add graceful rotation + backoff. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-04-02.

3) 2026-03-26 05:50 UTC — elevated GPU OOMs causing instance restarts in dedicated pool -> slow ramp and tail latency.
   - Root cause: model memory footprint under the new quantization profile slightly larger at runtime due to allocator fragmentation.
   - Mitigation: drained affected hosts and disabled the new quantization profile for affected model family.
   - Follow-ups: run memory profiling, adjust allocator flags, test quant profile in canary infra. Owner: Jordan. Due: 2026-04-07.

Proposed mitigations / discussion points for meeting:
- Short-term: tighten rollout script (linearize reloads), temporarily disable risky quant profiles in prod, and add a pre-rollout memory smoke test.
- Mid-term: improve canary isolation (run canary on dedicated isolated pool to avoid noisy reloads affecting steady-state), and add per-deployment warm-up traffic to prime caches.
- Observability: add a dashboard tile for model-reload events and a correlate view that shows recent deploys vs tail latency spikes.
- Alerting: tune latency alert thresholds to avoid low-SLO noise from known warm-up windows; add a suppression window around controlled rollouts.

Action items (owner - due):
- Samira: implement rollout gating + JIRA-SRE-987 (2026-04-05).
- Ethan: sync with infra-auth on key rotation/backoff (JIRA-AUTH-321) and propose changes (2026-04-02).
- Jordan: memory profiling for new quant profile and adjust allocator flags (2026-04-07).
- Observability (assigned: Priya?) : add model-reload dashboard and correlate panel (2026-04-09).
- On-call handbook: add a short-runbook for model reload storms and when to pause rollouts (owner: Jordan/Samira) (2026-04-03).

Notes / things to raise in meeting:
- Are product rollouts coordinating with SRE on canary windows? Need stricter pre-rollout checklist.
- Discussion around auto-fallback: should we route to older model variant automatically if reloads cause capacity issues? Risk/cost trade-off.
- Consider adding a small reserved headroom in Dedicated pools during major model changes to avoid capacity churn.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Do we have reliable signals to detect a reload-induced tail spike before client-visible errors? (need to test synthetic warm-up telemetry).
- Can deployment tooling be made aware of memory fragmentation heuristics (allocator flags per model build)?

Prep checklist for sync:
- Bring latest SLO chart snapshot (Samira)
- Bring deploy timeline & rollout logs for 03/25 (Jordan)
- Bring auth rotation timeline (Ethan)
- Draft rollout gating proposal (Samira)

Quick personal notes:
- Keep the meeting tight; prioritize clear owners and short due dates.
- Post-meeting: send summary + action items in #sre-ops and tag owners.

End of prep notes.

----
Scratch / backlog ideas (not for this meeting):
- Experiment: pre-warm cache using a small synthetic workload from regional edge to reduce first-request latency.
- Add synthetic traffic that checks model readiness after reloads (health-checks that include a lightweight generate).
- Explore OTA allocator tuning in collaboration with serving runtime team for fragmentation mitigation.
